title: [Bug] TypeError in usage_tracker.py: object of type 'int' has no len() when merging usage entries
author: chizukicn

comments.author: TomeHirata
comments.body: Thanks @chizukicn for the report. But I couldn't reproduce the issue with your example code, can you share mlflow version as well? I wonder when `usage_entry2` becomes `int`, which is not expected.

comments.author: chizukicn
comments.body:
Hi @TomeHirata , my MLflow version is the latest 3.7.0. The issue is not consistently reproducible, but in my environment it happens very frequently. Here is my setup: macOS 26.1, Python 3.13.

However, it seems that this problem is not related to MLflow or the environment. It’s caused specifically by the `_merge_usage_entries` function.
```
 [
  {
    "completion_tokens": 212,
    "prompt_tokens": 570,
    "total_tokens": 782,
    "completion_tokens_details": null, // here
    "prompt_tokens_details": null 
  },
  {
    "completion_tokens": 211,
    "prompt_tokens": 715,
    "total_tokens": 926,
    "completion_tokens_details": null,
    "prompt_tokens_details": null
  },
  {
    "completion_tokens": 264,
    "prompt_tokens": 421,
    "total_tokens": 685,
    "completion_tokens_details": {
      "accepted_prediction_tokens": null,
      "audio_tokens": null,
      "reasoning_tokens": 0,
      "rejected_prediction_tokens": null,
      "text_tokens": null,
      "image_tokens": null
    },
    "prompt_tokens_details": null
  }
]
```
After stepping through with breakpoints, I found that when a usage_entry that is supposed to be a dict is None, it first gets converted to 0 by the line:
```python
result[k] = (current_v or 0) + (v or 0)
```
Then, when this entry is merged with another usage_entry with the same key, the bug is triggered.

comments.author: TomeHirata
comments.body: I see, that makes sense. Can you update your pr to fix that line then?
